key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks identify plate orientations for near-isotropic, ultrastiff lattices, with at least six plates required and stiffness approaching the Hashin–Shtrikman upper bound.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a systematic route to lightweight, stiff architectures with nearly direction-independent elastic behavior, reducing reliance on heuristic design.
method: Apply PINNs to analytical equations to solve for plate orientations.
Assemble orientations into closed-cell, foam-like geometries and evaluate them with finite element simulations.
Additively manufacture six-plate lattices using LAPIS and characterize them experimentally.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stiffness reaching 90% of the Hashin–Shtrikman upper bound at relative density 0.4 and a near-isotropic Zener ratio of 0.95 at relative density 0.1.
watch_item: Suboptimal plate placement introduces bending, so orientation solutions alone do not guarantee bound-level stiffness in assembled geometries.
paper_title: Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
